# [D1 — Bottom trawling](../hypodrafts/D1.md "Bottom trawling")

*Generated by `scripts/pages/hypodraft_d1.py`: what the data held here can and cannot show about the hypothesis. Each marked statement links to what it rests on.*

**Draft, not a result.** <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-STATUS">The test this page specifies has not been run: no script in this repository computes it, and the fishing-effort layers it needs are not fetched.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-STATUS "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-ZIP">They are one archive on figshare, `2022_helcom_spatial_effort_intensity.zip`, of [23,051,366](../SOURCES.md#F-c465cc6907) bytes, under `CC BY 4.0`.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-ZIP "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The observable consequence, stated so it can fail

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-MECH">Read as an oxygen mechanism rather than a fauna one, [D1](../hypodrafts/D1.md "Bottom trawling") says gear dragged over fine reduced sediment resuspends sulphide and labile organic matter, which consume oxygen where they are released: at the bed, within weeks, **and only where fine reduced sediment exists.** Per station-quarter:</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-MECH "What this claim rests on")</sup>

1. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-P-WITHIN">**Within station.** Near-bed oxygen anomaly is lower in a station's own quarters following a high subsurface swept-area ratio (`subsur_sar`) in its c-square than in its own quarters following a low one, after removing station mean, month-of-year and year.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-P-WITHIN "What this claim rests on")</sup>
2. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-P-SUB">**Substrate interaction.** The effect is present on *Mud and sandy mud* / *Muddy sand* / *Quaternary clay and silt* and absent on *Sand* / *Gravel and coarse sand* / *Till/diamicton* / *Sedimentary rock*.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-P-SUB "What this claim rests on")</sup>
3. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-P-PLACEBO">**Placebo.** No comparable effect in near-**surface** oxygen at the same stations.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-P-PLACEBO "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-FALSIFY">**Falsified if:** the within-station coefficient lies inside the null distribution below; **or** the coarse-substrate coefficient is indistinguishable from the mud one; **or** the surface placebo moves with effort as strongly as the bed. The substrate interaction and the surface placebo are what make this a test of trawling rather than of where fish are.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-FALSIFY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The data held here, counted

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-PANEL">**The panel.** `docs/data/areas/stations_series.json`, the monthly panel this project analyses, holds [679,422](../SOURCES.md#F-b61d7944ec) station-months across its [9](../SOURCES.md#F-81bea72caf) variables at [1,415](../SOURCES.md#F-fff0060a3d) stations, over [564](../SOURCES.md#F-008df4b99b) months from [1980](../SOURCES.md#F-44433af5f2): one median per station, month and variable, so a station-quarter built from it is a median of medians. Near-bed oxygen (`oxy_bed`) fills [76,980](../SOURCES.md#F-a95c664ddf) station-months and near-surface oxygen (`oxy_surf`), the placebo, [76,963](../SOURCES.md#F-b25282f4f4).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-PANEL "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-FLUO">Fluorescence (`fluo`), the productivity covariate, fills [60,460](../SOURCES.md#F-9ecc204bb2) station-months. It is a sensor channel of the CTD cast, not the laboratory chlorophyll the water-chemistry extract carries separately as `Klorofyl a`, on [185,314](../SOURCES.md#F-d5e65e675b) rows.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-FLUO "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-OVERLAP">How many of the panel's station-months fall in the effort layers' years, at how many stations and in how many c-squares, is not counted by any script here: the overlap is the first thing the test must count.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-OVERLAP "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-META">**The effort layers.** HELCOM's metadata record for them says they are based on VMS data, processed by ICES's working group on spatial fisheries data (WGSFD) to c-square products, by year and by quarter; for the mobile bottom-contacting gear groups — dredge, demersal seine and otter trawl, and their total — they give swept area and the surface and subsurface swept-area ratio (`sur_sar`, `subsur_sar` in the shapefiles), and these, unlike weight, value and fishing hours, are never withheld for anonymity.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-META "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-SARMODEL">Swept-area ratio is computed, not observed; how fishing is told from steaming and how each gear's width is set is not described in either record pinned here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-SARMODEL "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-FLEET">Vessels without VMS are not in the layers, and which vessels carried it in these years is not established from any document pinned here, so how much of the inshore fleet is missing is unknown.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-FLEET "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-QUARTER">The layers are totals per c-square, gear group and quarter, so timing within a quarter is gone and the test's lag can only be a whole quarter.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-QUARTER "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-SEABED">**Substrate.** `data/raw/geus/seabed_sediment_dk.gpkg`, layer `Seabed_sedimen`, holds [108](../SOURCES.md#F-c4d0799598) polygons in [7](../SOURCES.md#F-6215d8e767) classes of the field `sedimenten`: Sand [22](../SOURCES.md#F-ab120cdc4e), Till/diamicton [22](../SOURCES.md#F-d1b701bcea), Gravel and coarse sand [22](../SOURCES.md#F-db52951fc0), Muddy sand [16](../SOURCES.md#F-e83415b0c0), Quaternary clay and silt [14](../SOURCES.md#F-a78103a379), Mud and sandy mud [9](../SOURCES.md#F-cd59077a96), Sedimentary rock [3](../SOURCES.md#F-858adbb0c7) — counts of polygons, not of area.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-SEABED "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-SCALE">The layer is compiled from surveys at map scales whose denominators, in the `scale` field, run from [5,000](../SOURCES.md#F-0827f1f9d3) to [500,000](../SOURCES.md#F-d20841b0ec), with [7](../SOURCES.md#F-7caf85939e) polygons at the finest scale and [7](../SOURCES.md#F-0fb797829f) at the coarsest, so boundary precision is not uniform.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-SCALE "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-BOUNDARY">Carry distance to a class boundary as a covariate, and test stations near a boundary separately.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-BOUNDARY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-POSITION">**Depth and position.** The CTD extract, `data/raw/oda/ctd.csv.gz` ([448.7](../SOURCES.md#F-71de5ceb31) MB compressed), has columns beside each station's coordinates (`X_UTM32`, `Y_UTM32`) for the depth (`Dybde (m)`) and the position (`MålingX_UTM32`, `MalingY_UTM32`) of each measurement row, so one streamed pass can place each cast in the c-square it was taken in, with its depth.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-POSITION "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-POSGAP">How often a measurement's position differs from its station's is not counted here.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-POSGAP "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## The null, under the constraint actually imposed

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-NULLWHY">The test has a spatial arm and a within-station arm, each with its own constraint and null, and **neither null is a plain shuffle.** Effort is spatially autocorrelated and so is bathymetry, and contiguity alone makes partitions agree: on this project's nearest-neighbour graph of [150](../SOURCES.md#F-36c69a2711) stations, random connected partitions with group sizes matched to the official water bodies agree with each other at a mean adjusted Rand index of [0.337](../SOURCES.md#F-a08dbf76c1) (`docs/data/areas/partition_contiguous.json`, `contiguous_null` in `scripts/partition_contiguous.py`), where the index corrects for chance against arbitrary partitions, not contiguous ones. A cell-wise shuffle of effort would repeat that mistake.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-NULLWHY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-NULL-SPATIAL">**Spatial arm** (cross-sectional, the weak one). Constraint: stations sit where they sit and effort has the structure it has. Null: keep the effort field whole and break only its *registration* with the stations — random rotations and toroidal translations within a Danish sea mask, rejecting draws that put more than [5](../SOURCES.md#F-92efc478ce)% of stations on no-data; plus a second null by `contiguous_null`-style connected block resampling on the c-square adjacency graph with matched block sizes. At least [999](../SOURCES.md#F-37fa5eca11) draws, reported against both.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-NULL-SPATIAL "What this claim rests on")</sup>
- <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-NULL-WITHIN">**Within-station arm** (primary). Constraint: station identity, month-of-year and year are absorbed. Null: circular shifts of each station's own effort series by whole years, plus a cluster bootstrap over stations. This preserves each station's effort marginal, the seasonal cycle and effort's serial correlation, breaking only the time alignment.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-NULL-WITHIN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## Procedure

1. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-S1">Fetch and unzip the archive named above; keep the mobile bottom-contacting gear groups the record lists; count the c-squares that intersect the stations' bounding box.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-S1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
2. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-S2">Assign each cast to its own c-square from its measurement coordinates; roll to station-quarter medians of the variables used below.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-S2 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
3. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-S3">Join `subsur_sar` of the *preceding* quarter; keep fluorescence same-quarter, not lagged.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-S3 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
4. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-S4">Fit near-bed oxygen on the lagged `log1p(subsur_sar)` with station, month and year fixed effects and covariates: fluorescence, near-bed temperature (solubility), near-bed salinity (stratification proxy), depth.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-S4 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
5. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-S5">Refit with a substrate × effort interaction; repeat the whole fit on surface oxygen as the placebo.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-S5 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
6. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-S6">Report every coefficient against both nulls above, never a textbook p-value.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-S6 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## What a result would, and would not, license

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-CONFOUND">The obvious confound: trawlers fish where fish are, and fish are where productivity is, so any raw effort–oxygen association is that association read backwards. The within-station fixed effect, fluorescence and the substrate interaction break it, and only together: the fixed effect removes everything time-invariant about a place (depth, substrate, mean productivity, distance from a source); fluorescence absorbs the time-varying part of the same confound; and the substrate interaction is a prediction the confound does not make, since productivity-driven effort would depress oxygen wherever trawlers work, while resuspension can only do it where reduced fines exist.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-CONFOUND "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-LICENSE">A mud-confined, bed-only coefficient outside both nulls would license exactly this: *trawling effort in the preceding quarter is associated with lower near-bed oxygen at Danish stations, 2016–2021, on fine substrate, beyond a null preserving the spatial and temporal structure of effort.* Not a budget attribution; not a causal claim (effort is not randomised, and a quarterly total cannot separate the trawl pass from what followed it); nothing about the fauna outcomes [O3](../HYPOTHESES.md "Loss of higher benthic life") and [O7](../HYPOTHESES.md "Loss of rooted vegetation"), since no fauna variable is here; nothing about vessels VMS does not see.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-LICENSE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-WEAK">A null result is weakly informative: quarterly effort, a computed swept-area ratio and vessels missing from the layers can each hide a real effect. And there is no baseline before trawling: the layers begin in 2016, so the test is a contrast across places and quarters, never a before-and-after.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-WEAK "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DZ-D1-CLUSTER">Stations that share a c-square share its effort, so effort is a shared regressor and errors must cluster on the c-square.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-DZ-D1-CLUSTER "What this claim rests on")</sup>
